extends: ACT/LAW machine contracts as a proposed extension; does not edit them

failure_handling.authority_expansion: refuse the intent; record the attempt as evidence (reputation input)
failure_handling.provenance_loss: fail closed; halt; do not proceed on the intent

law_integration.gained: new precondition — authorization valid only against a walkable, non-expanding provenance chain

predicates.authority_non_expansion: authority_at_hop_n must be a subset of authority_at_hop_(n-1); violation => refuse + record
predicates.collective_resolves: a chain ending at COLLECTIVE must name the mechanism that produced the intent; unresolvable => not an authority
predicates.modification_attributed: any change across a hop must appear in modifications; silent modification => corrupt record => fail closed
predicates.provenance_required: no provenance record => UNKNOWN-provenance => cannot authorize action (fail closed)
predicates.provenance_walkable: every hop resolves to a bound identity and stated authority; unwalkable hop => whole chain unwalkable => UNKNOWN-provenance

provenance.source: legacy document NAYANET: A Digital Civilization (working dialogue), Shawn Vibert (SmartNet->NayaNET era)

fields.type: bound actor identity who first formed the intent
bound actor identity who granted authority, with grant scope and expiry
ordered list: hop_actor, what_changed, authority_invoked, timestamp
ordered hop list: from -> to, timestamp, channel
authority present at each hop (non-expansion checkable)

smart_ledger.concept: the extended chain, persisted across executions — the memory of intelligence in action; 'the DNA of a trustworthy Superbrain'
smart_ledger.entry: the full chain for one intent, from originator to learning
smart_ledger.purpose: lets a cold successor or auditor answer: where did this instruction come from, and who was allowed to give it?

why: an agent's intent isn't necessarily sourced from its creator; intent can propagate through the network — the chain-of-authority problem
